financial_summary: Bsr Real Estate Invt Tr is a small-cap real estate business with a $398M market cap on $144M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -2.0pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 54% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $64M in free cash flow — roughly 45 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -9.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 11.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 7.8% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
